previous: r12: Savar chose A (Report card) as the easiest to read and understand quickly. He found the narrow centred sheet odd and the page crammed, and he liked B's ruler and strand meters.
decision: Which layout of the report card should we build: full-width rows, rows with the ruler and meters, panels, or a summary beside the detail?
primary_axis: layout and spacing of the report card (order and content held from A)
route: /report-prototype?variant=A2|A3|A4|A5 (A stays as the r12 reference; B-E stay for comparison)
invariants: A's section order: header table, overall level and scale, comparison, by area, number facts, the child's work, how we help, next step
A's content and sample data; every number labelled sample except the FSA figures
full page width, aligned with the site nav; more space between and inside sections than r12

options.name: Wide document
options.bet: The report card across the full width; each section is a row with its title and a one-line explanation on the left
options.benefit: Closest to A, with room to breathe; the left titles make the page easy to scan
options.risk: The left column is mostly empty on short sections

options.name: Report card + ruler
options.bet: A2's rows, B's big ruler in a colour band for the overall level, and a meter in every area row
options.benefit: Keeps A's easy table and adds B's visuals that Savar liked; the answer is clear at a glance
options.cost: The colour band and meters add visual weight
options.risk: Meters can look more precise than 8-10 questions per area

options.name: Panels
options.bet: The same order, each section in its own roomy soft-grey panel; how we help and the next step side by side
options.benefit: Clear separation between sections; calm and roomy
options.cost: Panels repeat the same shape down the page
options.risk: Can feel like an app page more than a report

options.name: Summary beside detail
options.bet: The level, ruler, comparison and plan buttons stay in view on the left; areas as large meters, facts, work and how we help scroll on the right
options.benefit: The answer and the next step are always visible; uses the laptop width
options.cost: On tablets it stacks into one column, so the plan buttons come before the detail
options.risk: Asks for a card before the parent has read the detail

evidence: Screens per option: <id>-behind-bc-stage1-1440, <id>-on-ontario-stage2-768, <id>-ahead-stage3-help-1440. No horizontal overflow in any of the 12 captures.
